EEI Corp Reports Steady Growth in Quarterly Trade Figures

MANILA, Philippines – EEI Corp, a key player in the country’s engineering and construction sector, reported steady trade figures for the first quarter of 2024, reflecting continued momentum in both domestic and overseas markets amid a stable economic environment.

The company posted total revenues of PHP 6.2 billion for the quarter ending March, a 4.3% increase from the same period last year. Officials attributed the growth to sustained demand for infrastructure and industrial projects, especially in Metro Manila and several provinces. EEI Corp’s export revenues from ongoing projects in Southeast Asia also contributed to the positive result.

“The first quarter performance demonstrates the resilience and adaptability of our teams, both locally and abroad,” said company president Roberto Santos in a statement. “We continue to see robust activity in the engineering and construction industry, supported by government infrastructure programs and private sector investments.”

Industry analysts said the figures were broadly in line with expectations. “The growth is moderate but consistent, which is a good sign given current market conditions,” noted Maria de la Cruz, an analyst at Metrocity Securities. She highlighted that EEI Corp’s diversified project portfolio has allowed it to weather fluctuations in individual markets.

According to the Philippine Construction Association, the industry has maintained a steady recovery following the disruptions of recent years. “Ongoing public works and the resurgence of large-scale commercial developments have bolstered the order books of major contractors,” said association spokesperson Leo Ramirez.

EEI Corp reported that ongoing projects include transport infrastructure, commercial complexes, and energy facilities. The company said its order backlog remains strong, with new contracts secured in the first quarter expected to support growth through the rest of the year.

Labor representatives welcomed the continued stability. “Our members are seeing consistent work opportunities and safe site conditions,” said Estrella Villanueva, president of the National Construction Workers’ Union.

EEI Corp said it remains committed to investing in workforce training, safety enhancements, and technology upgrades to maintain its competitive edge in the sector.
